subject: Physics
stem: In the given circuit ideal diodes are connected. Then the current through \(3\,\Omega\) resistance is
solution:
The upper plate of the cell is positive, so current leaves it through the \(2\,\Omega\) resistor.
\(D_1\) points downward, so it is forward biased and conducts through the \(3\,\Omega\) branch. \(D_2\) points upward, so it is reverse biased and its branch carries no current.
\(I = \frac{15}{2 + 3} = 3\,\text{A}\) through the \(3\,\Omega\) resistor.

stem: In a pure germanium intrinsic concentration is \(n_i = 10^{16}/\text{m}^3\) at 300 K. If \(10^{21}\) atoms of Boron are added to per cubic meter. The new electron concentration will be
solution:
Boron is trivalent, so the crystal becomes p-type with \(n_h \approx 10^{21}\,\text{m}^{-3}\).
Mass action law: \(n_e n_h = n_i^2\), so \(n_e = \frac{(10^{16})^2}{10^{21}} = 10^{11}\,\text{m}^{-3}\).

subject: Physics
stem: On increasing the temperature the specific resistance of a semiconductor
solution: On heating, more electrons cross the small band gap, so the number of charge carriers rises sharply and the resistivity of a semiconductor decreases.

subject: Physics

solution:
For silicon \(E_g = 1.1\,\text{eV} = 1.1 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} = 1.76 \times 10^{-19}\,\text{J}\).
So options 1 and 3 are the same value.

subject: Physics
stem: For given semiconductor contribution of current due to electron and hole is in ratio \(\frac{3}{1}\) and the ratio of drift velocity for electron and hole is \(\frac{5}{2}\), then calculate the ratio of electron to hole concentration.
solution:
\(I = neAv_d\), so \(\frac{I_e}{I_h} = \frac{n_e}{n_h} \cdot \frac{v_e}{v_h}\).
\(\frac{3}{1} = \frac{n_e}{n_h} \times \frac{5}{2}\), so \(\frac{n_e}{n_h} = \frac{6}{5}\).

subject: Physics
stem: A potential barrier of 0.5 V exists across a p-n junction. An electron with KE 2.5 eV approaches the p-n junction from p-side then the KE of electron as it enters n-side.
solution:
The junction field points from the n-side to the p-side, so it pushes an electron from the p-side towards the n-side.
The electron going from p to n therefore gains \(e \times 0.5\,\text{V} = 0.5\,\text{eV}\).
\(KE = 2.5 + 0.5 = 3\,\text{eV}\).

subject: Physics
stem: If current in given circuit is 0.2 A, then calculate resistance of P-N junction.
solution:
The diode is forward biased and in series with both resistors: \(I = \frac{V}{R + r}\).
\(0.2 = \frac{10}{20 + 10 + r}\), so \(30 + r = 50\) and \(r = 20\,\Omega\).

subject: Physics
stem: In the given circuit, if P-N junction is ideal, then calculate the current flowing through it.
solution:
In both cells the short plate is at the top, so the left end is at \(-2\,\text{V}\) and the right end at \(-4\,\text{V}\).
The diode's anode (\(-2\,\text{V}\)) is higher than the far side (\(-4\,\text{V}\)), so it is forward biased.
\(I = \frac{-2 - (-4)}{200} = \frac{2}{200} = 0.01\,\text{A}\).

subject: Physics

subject: Physics
stem: In given circuit determine \(I\), \(I_1\) and \(I_2\) is (in mA).
solution:
The diode at the far right points downward and is forward biased, so it shorts that point to the lower rail (0 V). The series diode is also forward biased, so the node after the \(4\,\text{k}\Omega\) resistor is at 0 V too.
Both \(10\,\text{k}\Omega\) resistors then have 0 V across them: \(I_1 = 0\).
\(I = I_2 = \frac{20}{4\,\text{k}\Omega} = 5\,\text{mA}\). So \(I, I_1, I_2 = 5, 0, 5\).

subject: Physics
stem: The electrical circuit used to get smooth DC output from a rectifier circuit is called
solution: A filter (a capacitor or an LC network) removes the AC ripple from the pulsating rectifier output and gives a smooth DC.

subject: Physics
stem: The circuit shown in the figure contains two diodes each with a forward resistance of \(50\,\Omega\) and with infinite reverse resistance. If the battery voltage is 6V, find the current through the \(100\,\Omega\) resistance is
solution:
Current leaves the + terminal on the left and goes up and to the right along the top. \(D_1\) points to the right, so it conducts; \(D_2\) points to the left, so it blocks.
Circuit: \(D_1\) (\(50\,\Omega\)) + \(150\,\Omega\) + \(100\,\Omega\) in series.
\(I = \frac{6}{50 + 150 + 100} = \frac{6}{300} = 0.02\,\text{A}\).

subject: Physics
stem: In the following figure, the diodes which are forward biased, are
solution:
A diode is forward biased when its p-side (triangle) is at higher potential than its n-side (bar).
(a) p-side at \(+10\,\text{V}\), n-side at \(+5\,\text{V}\): forward. (b) p-side at \(-10\,\text{V}\), n-side at 0 V: reverse.
(c) p-side at \(-5\,\text{V}\), n-side at \(-12\,\text{V}\): forward. (d) p-side at 0 V, n-side at \(+5\,\text{V}\): reverse.
So a and c.

subject: Physics
stem: In a P-N junction, potential barrier of 250 mV exists across junction. A hole with KE of 300 meV approaches junction from n-side. Find KE of hole when it crosses junction.
solution:
The junction field points from n to p, so a hole moving from the n-side to the p-side is pushed along by it and gains \(250\,\text{meV}\).
\(KE = 300 + 250 = 550\,\text{meV}\).

subject: Physics
stem: Find the charge on \(C_1\) capacitor if two ideal diodes are used in the circuit.
solution:
The vertical diode can conduct only upward, so it blocks the charging current; the series diode is forward biased.
So \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) charge in series across V: \(Q = \frac{C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2}V\).
In series both carry this same charge, so the charge on \(C_1\) is \(\frac{C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2}V\).

subject: Physics
stem:
**Assertion:** During reverse biasing, a diode doesn't conduct current.
**Reason:** It narrows the depletion layers.
options: Both assertion and reason are correct and reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
Both assertion and reason are correct but reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
Assertion is correct, but reason is incorrect
Assertion is incorrect but reason is correct
solution:
The assertion is true: a reverse-biased diode passes almost no current.
The reason is false: reverse bias widens the depletion layer; forward bias narrows it.

subject: Physics
stem: The V- I characteristics of silicon diode as shown. Then the resistance of diode when forward bias current is equal to 10 mA is
solution:
From the graph, \(I = 10\,\text{mA}\) at \(V = 0.5\,\text{V}\).
Resistance \(R = \frac{V}{I} = \frac{0.5}{10 \times 10^{-3}} = 50\,\Omega\).
reasoning: Options printed at top of p003_R.

subject: Physics
stem: Four silicon diodes are connected as shown in the figure. Assuming the diodes to be ideal, the current through the resistor R is
solution:
The upper plate of the cell is positive. In the left column the upper diode points down into the midpoint, and in the right column the lower diode points down to the lower rail.
So current flows: top rail, upper-left diode, R, lower-right diode, bottom rail. The other two diodes are reverse biased.
\(I = \frac{5}{50} = 0.1\,\text{A}\).

subject: Physics
stem:
**Assertion:** The resistivity of a typical semiconductor decreases with increase in temperature.
**Reason:** As temperature of a semi conductor increases, the number of charge carriers per unit volume increases.
options: Both assertion and reason are correct and reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
Both assertion and reason are correct but reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
Assertion is correct, but reason is incorrect
Assertion is incorrect but reason is correct
solution: Both are true. Heating frees more electron-hole pairs, so the carrier density rises, and that is exactly why the resistivity falls.

subject: Physics
stem: A potential barrier 'V' volts exists across a P-N junction. The thickness of the depletion region is 'd'. An electron with 'v' velocity approaches PN junction from N-side. The velocity of the electron crossing the junction is
solution:
An electron going from the N-side to the P-side moves against the barrier and loses energy \(eV\).
\(\frac{1}{2}mv'^2 = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 - eV\), so \(v' = \sqrt{v^2 - \frac{2Ve}{m}}\).

subject: Physics
stem: If the ratio of the concentration of electrons of that of holes in a semiconductor is \(\frac{7}{5}\) and that the ratio of currents is \(\frac{7}{4}\), then the ratio of drift velocity is
solution:
\(\frac{I_e}{I_h} = \frac{n_e}{n_h} \cdot \frac{v_e}{v_h}\), so \(\frac{7}{4} = \frac{7}{5} \cdot \frac{v_e}{v_h}\).
\(\frac{v_e}{v_h} = \frac{7}{4} \times \frac{5}{7} = \frac{5}{4}\).

subject: Physics
stem: In a semiconducting material \(\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^{\text{th}}\) of the total current is carried by the holes and the remaining is carried by the electrons. The drift speed of electrons is twice that of holes at this temperature, the ratio between the number densities of electrons and holes is
solution:
Holes carry \(\frac{1}{5}\) and electrons \(\frac{4}{5}\) of the current, so \(\frac{I_e}{I_h} = 4\).
\(4 = \frac{n_e}{n_h} \times 2\), so \(\frac{n_e}{n_h} = 2\).

subject: Physics
stem: Pure Si at 500 K has equal number of electron \((n_e)\) and hole \((n_h)\) concentrations of \(1.5 \times 10^{16}\,\text{m}^{-3}\). Doping by indium increases \(n_h\) to \(4.5 \times 10^{22}\,\text{m}^{-3}\). The doped semiconductor is of
solution:
Indium is trivalent, so the material is p-type.
\(n_e = \frac{n_i^2}{n_h} = \frac{(1.5 \times 10^{16})^2}{4.5 \times 10^{22}} = \frac{2.25 \times 10^{32}}{4.5 \times 10^{22}} = 5 \times 10^{9}\,\text{m}^{-3}\).

subject: Physics
stem:
The barrier potential of a p-n junction depends on
(1) type of semiconductor material
(2) amount of doping
(3) temperature
Which one of the following is correct?
solution: The barrier potential depends on the material (Si about 0.7 V, Ge about 0.3 V), on the doping level (heavier doping gives a larger barrier) and on temperature (it falls as temperature rises). So all three.
reasoning: Sub-items are printed numbered 1) 2) 3); written as (1) (2) (3) to match the options.

subject: Physics
stem: Choose the correct statement.
options: The breakdown in reverse biased p-n junction is more likely to occur due large velocity of minority carriers if the doping concentration is small.
The breakdown in reverse biased p-n junction is more likely to occur due to strong electric field in the depletion region if doping concentration is large.
solution:
Lightly doped junctions break down by avalanche: minority carriers gain large speeds and ionise atoms by collision, so statement 1 is right.
Heavily doped junctions have a thin depletion layer with a very strong field that pulls electrons out of bonds (Zener breakdown), so statement 2 is right.
The band gap of Ge is about 0.7 eV, so statement 3 is right too.

subject: Physics
stem:
**Assertion:** Germanium is preferred over silicon for making semiconductor devices.
**Reason:** Energy gap for Ge is more than that of Si.
options: both assertion and reason are true and the reason is correct explanation of the assertion
both assertion and reason are true but reason is not correct explanation of the assertion
assertion is true, but the reason is false
both assertion and reason are false
solution:
Silicon, not germanium, is preferred: its larger gap (1.1 eV against about 0.7 eV for Ge) gives a smaller leakage current and better behaviour at higher temperature.
So the assertion is false and the reason (Ge gap larger than Si) is also false.

subject: Physics
stem: Which one of the following statements is not correct?
options: A diode does not obey Ohm's law
A PN junction diode symbol shows an arrow identifying the direction of current flow in forward bias
An ideal diode acts as an open switch in forward bias
An ideal diode acts as an open switch in reverse bias
solution: An ideal diode is a closed switch (zero resistance) in forward bias and an open switch in reverse bias. So the statement that it is an open switch in forward bias is not correct.

subject: Physics
stem: On increasing the reverse bias voltage to a large value in a PN junction diode, current
solution: At the breakdown voltage, Zener or avalanche breakdown sets in and the reverse current increases suddenly while the voltage stays nearly constant.

subject: Physics
stem: The potential barrier existing across an unbiased p-n junction is 0.2 volt. What minimum kinetic energy a hole should have to diffuse from the p-side to the n-side if the junction is forward biased at 0.1 volt?
solution:
A forward bias of 0.1 V lowers the barrier from 0.2 V to \(0.2 - 0.1 = 0.1\,\text{V}\).
A hole crossing from p to n must climb this barrier, so it needs at least \(0.1\,\text{eV}\).

subject: Physics
stem:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
**Assertion (A):** If the temperature of a semiconductor is increased, its resistance decreases.
**Reason (R):** The energy gap between conduction band and valence band in case of semiconductor is large.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: both assertion and reason are true and the reason is correct explanation of the assertion
both assertion and reason are true but reason is not correct explanation of the assertion
assertion is true, but the reason is false
assertion is false, but the reason is true
solution:
The assertion is true: heating creates more carriers, so the resistance of a semiconductor falls.
The reason is false: the gap in a semiconductor is small (about 1 eV), which is why heating can excite electrons across it.

reasoning: '1 ppm' has a pencil stroke over it; the printed text reads 1 ppm.

subject: Physics
stem: In the given circuit, each diode has forward resistance of \(20\,\Omega\) and infinite backward resistance resistors and \(R_1 = R_2 = R_3 = 50\,\Omega\). The current through \(R_3\) is
solution:
The long plate of the 6 V cell is on the left, so current goes up the left side and to the right along the top branches.
\(D_2\) and \(D_3\) face each other, so the middle branch never conducts. \(D_1\) is forward biased.
\(I = \frac{6}{20 + 50 + 50} = \frac{6}{120} = 0.05\,\text{A} = 50\,\text{mA}\).
reasoning: Stem on p005_L, figure and options at top of p005_R.

subject: Physics
stem: When a selective impurity is doped into an intrinsic semiconductor, the conductivity of semiconductor
solution: Doping adds a large number of free electrons or holes, so the carrier density and hence the conductivity increase.

subject: Physics
stem: In the given circuit, the current through the battery will be
solution:
The long plate of the 8 V cell is on the right, so current goes up through \(2\,\Omega\) and leftward through \(D_1\), which conducts in that direction.
In the parallel block, \(D_2\) conducts only upward, so the downward current takes only the plain \(3\,\Omega\) branch.
\(I = \frac{8}{2 + 3 + 3} = 1\,\text{A}\).

subject: Physics
stem: Choose the correct statement regarding n-type semiconductor.
options: Current is mainly due to electrons
The number of electron in conduction band are equal to number of holes in valence band
solution:
In an n-type semiconductor electrons are the majority carriers, so the current is mainly due to electrons.
Every donor electron leaves behind a fixed positive ion, so the crystal as a whole stays neutral. Electrons far outnumber holes, so statement 3 is false.

subject: Physics
stem: If a full wave rectifier circuit is operating from 50 Hz mains, the fundamental frequency in the ripple will be
solution: A full wave rectifier gives one output pulse for each half cycle, so the ripple frequency is \(2f = 2 \times 50 = 100\,\text{Hz}\).

subject: Physics
stem: A 110 V AC supply is connected between points A and B as shown in the figure. The potential difference \(V_0\) across the capacitor is
solution:
The diode lets the capacitor charge to the peak of the AC and stops it from discharging back.
\(V_0 = V_{\text{peak}} = \sqrt{2} V_{\text{rms}} = 110\sqrt{2}\,\text{V}\).

subject: Physics
stem: The voltage at \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) of the arrangement shown in the figure will be respectively (cut-in voltage of diodes is 0.6 v)
solution:
\(D_1\) has +6 V on its p-side and the 3 V resistor end below, so it conducts: \(V_2 = 6 - 0.6 = 5.4\,\text{V}\).
\(D_2\) has its p-side at \(V_2 = 5.4\,\text{V}\) and its n-side pulled up to +6 V through \(10\,\text{k}\Omega\), so it is reverse biased and carries no current.
No drop across \(10\,\text{k}\Omega\), so \(V_1 = 6\,\text{V}\).

subject: Physics
stem: In the circuit shown in figure if the diode forward voltage drop is 0.3 v, then the voltage difference between A and B is
solution:
In steady DC the capacitor carries no current, so the 0.2 mA flows through both resistors and the diode.
\(V_{AB} = 0.2 \times 10^{-3} \times (5 + 5) \times 10^{3} + 0.3 = 2 + 0.3 = 2.3\,\text{V}\).

subject: Physics
stem: Find \(V_{AB}\).
solution:
The upper plate is positive and the diode points away from the middle node, so it is forward biased.
The two lower \(10\,\Omega\) resistors are then in parallel: \(5\,\Omega\). Total \(= 10 + 5 = 15\,\Omega\).
\(I = \frac{30}{15} = 2\,\text{A}\), so \(V_{AB} = 2 \times 5 = 10\,\text{V}\).

subject: Physics
stem:
**Assertion:** V - I characteristic of PN junction diode is same as that of any other conductor.
**Reason:** Semiconductor behaves like insulator at absolute zero.
options: Both assertion and reason are correct and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
Both assertion and reason are correct but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
Assertion is correct and reason is incorrect
Assertion is incorrect and reason is correct
solution:
The assertion is false: a diode's V-I curve is non-linear and different in the two directions, unlike an ohmic conductor.
The reason is true: at 0 K there are no free carriers, so a semiconductor behaves as an insulator.

subject: Physics
stem:
Which of the following statement is correct?
**Statement I:** Si and GaAs are preferred materials for solar cell.
**Statement II:** Semiconductors with band gap close to 2.8 eV are ideal materials for solar cell fabrication.
**Statement III:** Gallium Arsenide - phosphide is used for making LEDs of different colours.
solution:
I is true: Si (1.1 eV) and GaAs (1.43 eV) are preferred for solar cells.
II is false: the ideal gap is about 1.5 eV, close to the peak of solar radiation, not 2.8 eV.
III is true: GaAsP is used for LEDs of different colours. So I and III.

subject: Physics
stem: A doped semiconductor is
solution: Each impurity atom is neutral when added; the extra carrier it gives is balanced by its ion. So a doped semiconductor is electrically neutral.

subject: Physics
stem:
Which of the following statements are true?
A) the resistance of intrinsic semiconductors decreases with increase of temperature.
B) Doping pure silicon with trivalent impurities gives p-type semiconductor
C) The majority carriers in N-type semiconductors are holes
D) there are no free electrons at 0K in a semiconductor
options: A, B and D are true
solution:
A is true: an intrinsic semiconductor gains carriers on heating. B is true: trivalent doping gives a p-type material.
C is false: the majority carriers in an n-type material are electrons. D is true: at 0 K no electron is in the conduction band.
reasoning: Runs from p007_L onto p007_R.

subject: Physics
stem: In a pn junction diode, the depletion region is 400 nm wide and an electric field of \(5 \times 10^{5}\) v/m exists in it. The minimum kinetic energy of a conduction electron which can diffuse from n-side to p-side is
solution:
Barrier potential \(V = Ed = 5 \times 10^{5} \times 400 \times 10^{-9} = 0.2\,\text{V}\).
The electron must climb this barrier, so its minimum KE is \(0.2\,\text{eV}\).

subject: Physics
stem:
**Assertion:** Photodiodes are preferably used in reverse bias condition for measuring light intensity.
**Reason:** Fractional change in minority charge carriers due to photo-effects, dominated reverse bias current is more easily measurable than fractional change in forward bias current.
options: Both assertion and reason are correct and reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
Both assertion and reason are correct but reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
Assertion is correct, but reason is incorrect
Assertion is incorrect but reason is correct
solution: Both are true. Light changes the minority carrier density by a large fraction of the small reverse current, so the change is easy to measure, whereas in forward bias the same change is lost in the large majority current. That is why photodiodes are used in reverse bias.
reasoning: Printed 'perferbly' corrected to 'preferably'; 'charge carries' corrected to 'charge carriers'.

subject: Physics
stem: The values of currents \(I\), \(I_1\) and \(I_2\) respectively in the given circuit is (diodes are ideal)
solution:
Reading the bottom resistor as \(20\,\Omega\). The long plate of the 5 V cell is on the left, so current goes left through \(20\,\Omega\) and up the left side: this is I.
\(D_1\) points right and conducts. \(D_2\) points left, so the top branch is blocked: \(I_2 = 0\).
\(I = I_1 = \frac{5}{20 + 30} = 0.1\,\text{A}\).
reasoning: In the figure the bottom resistor is labelled '20 V' (likely a misprint for 20 ohm); the battery is 5 V.

subject: Physics
stem: If the forward voltage in a semiconductor diode is changed from 0.5 V to 2V, then forward current changes by 1.5 mA. The forward resistance of diode will be
solution: \(r = \frac{\Delta V}{\Delta I} = \frac{2 - 0.5}{1.5 \times 10^{-3}} = \frac{1.5}{1.5 \times 10^{-3}} = 1000\,\Omega = 1\,\text{k}\Omega\).

subject: Physics
stem:
**Assertion (A):** When the temperature of a semiconductor is increased, then its conductance increases.
**Reason (R):** The energy gap between conduction band and valence band semiconductor is small.
options: Both assertion and reason are correct and reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
Both assertion and reason are correct but reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
Assertion is correct, but reason is incorrect
Assertion is incorrect but reason is correct
solution: Both are true. Because the gap is small, heating can lift many electrons into the conduction band, so the conductance rises. The reason explains the assertion.

subject: Physics
stem: The width of forbidden gap in silicon crystal is 1.1 eV. When the crystal is converted to a n-type semiconductor, the distance of fermi level from conduction band is
solution:
In pure silicon the Fermi level is at the middle, \(\frac{1.1}{2} = 0.55\,\text{eV}\) below the conduction band.
Donor doping moves it up towards the conduction band, so the distance becomes less than 0.55 eV.

subject: Physics
stem: Which of following is incorrect?
options: In reverse bias the flow of current through diode is mainly due to drift current
In forward bias resistance offered by the diode is less and width of depletion layer is also less
In reverse bias of an ideal diode, the resistance offered is zero
solution: An ideal diode in reverse bias offers infinite resistance, not zero. Statements 1 to 3 are correct: the diode is non-ohmic, the small reverse current is a drift of minority carriers, and forward bias narrows the depletion layer and lowers the resistance.

subject: Physics
stem:
**Statement I:** LEDs consume low power for their operation.
**Statement II:** For LEDs no warm up time required and have long life compared to incandescent bulbs.
options: I is true and II is false
I is false and II is true
Both I and II are false
solution: Both are true. LEDs work at low voltage and current, switch on instantly with no warm up, and last much longer than incandescent bulbs.

subject: Physics

subject: Physics

stem: Choose the correct option about the breakdown voltage in a zener diode.
options: It decreases when electric current increases
It equals the electric current times the resistance
solution: In breakdown the voltage across a Zener diode stays practically constant over a wide range of current; that is why it is used as a voltage regulator.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Zener diode and opto-electronic junction devices
stem: Figure shows Zener diode used as a voltage regulator with a break down voltage of 40 V connected to 100 V DC source with a series resistance \(R_S\) and a load resistor \(R_L\) find the output voltage across \(R_L\).
solution:
The 100 V supply is well above the 40 V breakdown voltage, so the Zener works in breakdown and holds the voltage across itself constant.
\(R_L\) is in parallel with the Zener, so the output voltage is 40 V.

solution: In avalanche breakdown the minority carriers are accelerated by the reverse field, collide with atoms and knock out more electron-hole pairs, which multiply in a chain. So it is due to collisions of minority carriers. A strong field alone in a thin depletion layer is the Zener mechanism.

solution:
Look at the orientation first. The long plate of the battery is at the top, so current leaves the top terminal and flows down through the zener, and the zener's arrow points down: it is **forward biased**. A forward-biased zener conducts like an ordinary diode, so its breakdown voltage (10 V) plays no part.
The diode is nearly a short, so almost no current goes through \(R_L\), and almost all of it goes through the zener:
\(I \approx \frac{60\,\text{V}}{4\,\text{k}\Omega} = 15\,\text{mA}\).
(Had the zener been reverse biased, it would hold 10 V and carry \(\frac{60 - 10}{4} - \frac{10}{2} = 7.5\,\text{mA}\); that is the trap.)
